pick.headline: Gamsakhurdia's Round Table wins Georgia's elections
pick.summary: On October 28, 1990, Georgia's first multi-party elections were won by the Round Table bloc of the nationalist Zviad Gamsakhurdia.
pick.significance: Georgia's vote put a pro-independence government in power in a Soviet republic.
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of October 30, 1990, carried Moscow TASS in English: unofficial results showed Gamsakhurdia's Round Table-Free Georgia bloc emerging as the leading force, winning 34 districts to the Communists' 22.

alternates.headline: Felipe Gonzalez's Socialists win Spanish elections
alternates.summary: On October 28, 1982, the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party led by Felipe Gonzalez won a landslide in the general election.
alternates.significance: It was the first left-wing government in Spain since the civil war, and came eighteen months after a failed coup.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of October 29, 1982, carried Panama City ACAN on Nicaragua's junta celebrating "as its own" the Spanish Socialist Workers Party's election victory, with its telegram to Felipe Gonzalez.
